questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Reason for a Discontinuity
questions.problem:
For what reason does the function $f(x)$ below have a discontinuity at $x=-2?$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+2}{2}, & x<-2 \\ 5, & x=-2 \\ \frac{18}{{x}^{2}+2}, & x>-2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's check the conditions necessary for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-2.$

- $f(-2)=5,$ so $f(-2)$ exists. $✓$

- We calculate the one-sided limits and find that they coincide:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}(\frac{{x}^{2}+2}{2}) \\  & =\frac{(-2)^{2}+2}{2} \\  & =3, \\ {lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}(\frac{18}{{x}^{2}+2}) \\  & =\frac{18}{(-2)^{2}+2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the overall limit exists and ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=3.\,\,✓$ $\,\,\,$

- The limit of the function is not equal to the function value: ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=3,$ while $f(-2)=5.$ $\times $

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=-2$ because ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)\ne f(-2).$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the function $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=-2$ because ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)\ne f(-2).$

questions.problem:
For what reason does the function $f(x)$ given below have a discontinuity at $x=-1?$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{2}, & x<-1 \\ 2, & x=-1 \\ \frac{2}{{x}^{2}+1}, & x>-1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's check the conditions necessary for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-1.$

- $f(-1)=2,$ so $f(-1)$ exists. $✓$

- We calculate the one-sided limits and check if they coincide:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}(\frac{{x}^{2}+1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{(-1)^{2}+1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1+1}{2} \\  & =1, \\ {lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}+1}) \\  & =\frac{2}{(-1)^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{2}{1+1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the overall limit exists and ${lim}_{x\to (-1)}f(x)=1$ $✓$

- The limit of the function is not equal to the function value: ${lim}_{x\to (-1)}f(x)=1,$ while $f(-1)=2.$ $\,\,\times $

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=-1$ because ${lim}_{x\to (-1)}f(x)\ne f(-1).$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the function $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=-1$ because ${lim}_{x\to (-1)}f(x)\ne f(-1).$
